t: Oghuz Turks from the Central Asian steppe, the Seljuks built an empire from Khorasan to the Mediterranean and became protectors of Sunni Islam.
Their victory at Manzikert opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement, paving the way for the Ottomans and helping provoke the Crusades.
With no fixed succession, the empire splintered after 1092; Qara Khitai and Khwarazmian blows ended the Great Seljuk line by 1194.
dyk: The poet and mathematician Omar Khayyam worked under Seljuk patronage on the Jalali solar calendar of 1079, more accurate than the Julian calendar.
ev: Tughril and Chaghri take Merv and Nishapur, throwing off Ghaznavid authority
Tughril and Chaghri rout the Ghaznavid sultan Masud I at Dandanaqan
Tughril enters Baghdad and is recognised as sultan by the Abbasid caliph
Alp Arslan defeats and captures the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV at Manzikert
Vizier Nizam al-Mulk is assassinated and Malik Shah dies weeks later, sparking civil war
The Qara Khitai defeat Sultan Sanjar at the Battle of Qatwan
Sanjar's death ends the eastern Seljuk line
The Khwarazm Shah Tekish kills Toghrul III, extinguishing the Great Seljuks
